Petitioners who are arraigned as accused No.1 and 2 and who are working as the Branch Manager and Managing Director of St.Milagres Credit Souhardha Co-operative Society Limited, Shantinagar,
Hubballi under Section 438 Cr.P.C. seeking anticipatory bail for the offences punishable under Sections 406, 420 and 417 Indian Penal Code.

entities.text: St.Milagres Credit Souhardha Co-operative Society Limited, Shantinagar
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: 2. Petitioners have contended that they are innocent of the offences alleged.
A false case has been registered against them.

The complaint averments shows that it is an attempt made by the complainant in collusion with the then Manager who was in-charge of withdrawal as well as cheque slips to falsely implicate the petitioners.
The then Manager has deliberately not maintained the records properly.
If complainant was not sanctioned loan of Rs.40,00,000/-, there was no need for the complainant to repay Rs.63,00,000/- which is inclusive of the interest.
This itself goes to show that it is a false complaint.
The dispute is civil in nature.
The petitioners have co-operated with the Investigating Officer and apprise them of the facts.
The petitioners are ready and willing to abide by any conditions that may be imposed and prays to allow the petition.

3. Learned High Court Government Pleader submitted oral objections stating that based on the complaint filed by one B.V.Iragar, investigation is taken up and it reveals that in their capacity as the Branch Manager and the Managing Director, petitioners/accused persons have cheated several account holders to the tune of Rs.1,10,00,000/- under the guise of sanctioning loan and further details are yet to be ascertained and they are not co-operating with the Investigating Officers to ascertain whether the loan sanctioned was credited to the account of the account holders and that they have withdrawn the same.
Their custodial presence is required for investigation.

2 question is committed by the previous manager, nothing prevents the petitioners from placing the said documents on record.

sentences.text: On account of non- cooperation of the petitioners, the investigation could not be proceeded with and prays to reject the petition.

4. Heard the arguments and perused the records.
5.
It is not in dispute that petitioners are the Branch Manager and Managing Director of St.Milagres Credit Souhardha Co-operative Society Limited, Hubballi.

entities.text: St.Milagres Credit Souhardha Co-operative Society Limited
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The investigation is taken up based on complaint filed by one B.V.Iragar.
The complaint averments reveal that in March, 2017, he approached the bank for loan to purchase a site.

However, the then manager convinced him that loan would be granted not only for purchase of site but also for construction of house and a total sum of Rs.40,00,000/- was granted based on mortgage with deposit of title deeds, but only Rs.11,00,000/- towards purchase of site was released with an assurance that
if he is not interested in utilizing the balance amount and repays the part of the loan which he has utilized his loan account would be closed.

However, after some time when he wanted to sell the site, he realized that Rs.63,74,226/- was due and since he was intending to sell the site, he deposited the entire amount and got released the charge created over the said property.
However when he went to the bank to get back the blank cheques and other documents given by him, he realized that the same have been misused and the loan amount was withdrawn from his account.
6. Based on the complaint, the concerned police have initiated investigation.

During the course of the investigation, the concerned police found that though petitioners have received a sum of Rs.1,10,00,000/- from IDBI Bank, Gokul Road which was supposed to be credited to the account of complainant and others, they have misappropriated a sum of Rs.30,13,000/- from the account of complainant, Rs.22,06,000/- from the account of Kasturi Hucchannavar and Rs.23,20,000/- from the account of one Gopal Pujar.
7.
The petitioners are contending that the alleged misappropriation, if any, is committed by the previous manager and he has left the job after tendering resignation.

If at all the said misappropriation is committed before petitioner No.1 took charge of the bank and that petitioner No.2 in his capacity as the Managing Director has no role in the said misappropriation, they are at liberty to produce the necessary records before the concerned police and become witnesses.

8. The main grievance of the Investigating Officer is that the petitioners are not producing the debit slip through which the loanees have allegedly withdrawn the loan amount credited to their account.

If at all it is the loanees who have withdrawn the loan amount from their account, there was no impediment for petitioners to place the said documents before the Investigating Officer and co-operate with him in finding the real culprit.

Having regard to the nature of the allegations made against the petitioners, their custodial presence is very much necessary to unearth the misdeeds committed while granting loan to the unsuspecting customers of the bank.

Certainly this is not a fit case to grant anticipatory bail to the petitioners and accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition is rejected.
